title: Probe first, then fine-tune: one extra opening epoch trains only the head on the FROZEN ImageNet trunk, so the random tile head's first gradients cannot distort the borrowed eyes (LP-FT)
hypothesis: Every large step on the held-out truedop_2024 photograph in this era came from the ImageNet-pretrained trunk (exp 12: 10.75% -> 49.5% usable; exp 16 MobileNetV2: 86.75%; exp 19 EfficientNet-B0: 92.5%), i.e. what transfers to a never-seen survey is the invariance the trunk brought from a million photographs, not what it learned from three. Experiment 20 (champion, 0.078: usable 93.0%, false 0.75%, abstain 6.25%) shows that how the trunk is TRAINED still matters out-of-domain: a better point on the same trajectory bought 0.5 points of usable and cut false fixes from 1.0% to 0.75% while the three training photographs stayed at 100%. The size gate (31.7 MB of 33.6 MB) closes the capacity road, so the remaining lever is the fine-tuning procedure. Today the trunk is fine-tuned from step 1 jointly with a RANDOMLY INITIALISED head (prototypes std 0.01 over 2,970 tiles, random 1x1 lifts, random embed BatchNorm): the earliest, largest gradients reaching the pretrained blocks are noise from a head that does not yet know any tile, and their trunk BatchNorm running stats start adapting at the same moment. Kumar et al. (ICLR 2022, 'Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution') prove and measure exactly this: full fine-tuning from a random head distorts the pretrained features along the directions the in-domain data uses and leaves the rest behind, which costs out-of-distribution accuracy (~7-10 points OOD on their benchmarks) while in-distribution accuracy is unchanged or better; training the head first on the frozen trunk (linear probe, then fine-tune: LP-FT) removes most of that loss. That is our split precisely: in-domain saturated at 100%, out-of-domain at 93%. Nothing in this era (searched hypothesis/method for freeze/probe/warm-up: none) nor in the 83 earlier experiments ever trained the head before the trunk; the trunk's training procedure since exp 12 has been 'fine-tune at 0.1x from step 1' unchanged. Builds on experiment 20 (the champion) with architecture, graph, losses, augmentation, MixStyle, committee, the fine-tune schedule and weight averaging all unchanged.
method: model/train.py only: prepend HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS = 1 extra epoch before the existing fine-tuning run. During it every member's pretrained trunk (m.trunk: EfficientNet-B0 features[0..7]) is frozen — requires_grad False on all trunk parameters and m.trunk kept in eval mode, so its BatchNorm running stats stay at their ImageNet values and stochastic depth is off — and only the head parameters (both 1x1 lifts, embed BatchNorm1d, prototypes, offset head) train, at the head LR 1e-3, with the same losses, augmentation, MixStyle and paired-survey batches as today. After that epoch the trunk is unfrozen and the existing EPOCHS-epoch run follows exactly as now (trunk at 0.1x, cosine LR multiplier 1.0 -> 0.1 over those EPOCHS epochs, weight averaging from fine-tune epoch EPOCHS//2+1, BN recalibration, export). Total epochs = EPOCHS + 1; the warm-up epoch is cheaper than a normal one (no trunk backward).
expected_outcome: Predicted on truedop_2024: mission 0.078 -> ~0.050-0.065; usable_fix_rate 93.0% -> ~94-95.5% (gain mostly from abstentions converting to usable fixes, as each member's tile belief on a foreign photograph rides less-distorted ImageNet features and the two members agree more often), false_fix_rate at or below 0.75%, abstain 6.25% -> ~4-5%. train_capture_diagnostics stay ~100% usable (LP-FT does not cost in-domain accuracy); median error ~36 m unchanged; model size and latency identical (same graph). Logged signals to read: after the warm-up epoch, top1 on the training views should already be substantial (frozen ImageNet GAP features + MLP lift can separate many tiles) — if it is near zero, the probe phase was too short to give the fine-tune a good head and the experiment tests less than intended; the end-of-run survey_diag xs_cos_same / xsurvey_agree should be at or above experiment 20's. Refutation: 2024 usable flat or down with the training diagnostics unchanged says feature distortion by the random head is not what limits the survey gap at this point (plausibly because the 0.1x trunk LR and weight averaging already protect the features), and that the remaining 7% abstentions need new information (more photographs, a different view of the frame) rather than a gentler fine-tune.
init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), head linear-probed on the frozen trunk for 1 epoch, then fine-tuned at 0.1x LR
eli5: The model's 'eyes' were borrowed from a network that had already looked at a million everyday photos, and that borrowed vision is what lets it recognise Berlin in a photograph it has never seen. Until now we started teaching the eyes and the brand-new 'map-reading' part at the same moment — so in the first hours the confused new part was yanking the borrowed eyes around. Now the map-reading part first practises for one round with the eyes held still, and only then are both tuned together, so the eyes keep more of what made them useful.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: the 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0 (pre-trained on ImageNet, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned on Berlin; each reads a 112-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map, each lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame into a 112-number place description; the weights carried are the average of the many versions visited over the second half of training

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: probe first, then fine-tune. One extra opening epoch trains only the map-reading parts (lifts, tile directions, offset head) while the borrowed ImageNet eyes are held completely still (weights and normalisation statistics frozen). Then the usual 8 epochs follow unchanged: cross-survey style mixing, angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, and the average of the second half's weights is what flies

implementation_brief:
Edit model/train.py ONLY. model/model.py is untouched (graph, parameter count, ONNX export identical to experiment 20).

1. Add a module constant next to AVG_EVERY: `HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS = 1  # extra opening epoch(s): head trains on the FROZEN pretrained trunk (LP-FT)`.

2. run_epoch(): add a keyword argument `freeze_trunk: bool = False`. Right after its existing `model.train()` call (line ~393), if freeze_trunk: for each member `m.trunk.eval()` (BN running stats frozen at ImageNet values, stochastic depth off). MixStyle is a separate module on the Member (not inside m.trunk), so it stays in train mode and keeps mixing — that is intended. Gradients: in train_area, before the warm-up epoch(s), set `p.requires_grad_(False)` for every parameter in trunk_params; after them, set `requires_grad_(True)` again. Do not otherwise change run_epoch's loss, targets, augmentation, statistics or bf16-autocast logic. Make sure nothing in the step depends on trunk params having .grad (Adam simply skips params whose grad is None; if there is any gradient clipping or grad-norm logging over all params, it must tolerate None grads). Also make sure survey_diag() and recalibrate_bn() — which call model.train()/model.eval() themselves — are unaffected: the trunk is re-put in train mode by the next run_epoch's model.train() once freeze_trunk is False.

3. train_area(): build the optimiser and LambdaLR exactly as now (two groups: trunk at 1e-3*TRUNK_LR_MULT, head at 1e-3; multiplier 0.1 + 0.9*0.5*(1+cos(pi*e/epochs)) where `epochs` is the CLI value). Before the existing `for epoch in range(epochs)` loop, add a warm-up loop `for w in range(HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS)` that: freezes trunk grads, calls run_epoch(..., averager=None, freeze_trunk=True), does NOT call sched.step() (so the head runs at constant 1e-3 and the fine-tune schedule starts fresh at multiplier 1.0 afterwards), runs survey_diag, and prints a log line in the same format as the existing per-epoch line but prefixed `[area] warmup (frozen trunk) {w+1}/{HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS}` with loss, top1, mean_max_softmax, member_top1, agree_rate and the survey_diag fields. Then unfreeze (requires_grad_(True) on all trunk params) and run the existing fine-tune loop COMPLETELY unchanged: same `epochs` count, same sched.step() per epoch, same averaging start `avg_start = epochs // 2` (0-based index within the fine-tune loop), same BN recalibration and export. Note: Adam has no state for the trunk params after warm-up (they never had grads), so its moment estimates start fresh at unfreeze — that is fine and intended; do NOT rebuild the optimiser (the head's Adam state should carry over).

4. Returned metrics dict: keep every existing key; set "epochs" to the CLI fine-tune epochs value and add "head_warmup_epochs": HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS, "total_epochs": epochs + HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS, "warmup_top1" (top1 at the end of the warm-up epoch), "warmup_member_top1", "warmup_agree_rate", "warmup_clean_top1" (from its survey_diag). Update "init" to "pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), head linear-probed on the frozen trunk for HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS epoch(s), then fine-tuned at 0.1x LR" and append ", head-only warm-up epoch on the frozen trunk before fine-tuning (LP-FT)" to "capture_sampling". n_train_crops / distinct_vantages_seen should count the warm-up epoch too ((epochs + HEAD_WARMUP_EPOCHS) * len(crops) * n_caps).

5. Add a short 'HEAD WARM-UP (experiment 21)' paragraph to the train.py module docstring describing the above, in the style of the existing per-experiment paragraphs.

Contracts to preserve (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI unchanged — `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket K] [--seed S]`, writing <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx; the ONNX contract in model/model.py's docstring — input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1]; export via model.model.export_onnx unchanged. Training must read only buckets(meta, "train") / the existing load_scene() — nothing may open the truedop_2024 eval capture in any form. Keep all per-view work on the device and add no .item()/.cpu() host syncs inside the step loop. Keep weight averaging, BN recalibration, MixStyle, committee, augmentation, margin loss and the bf16-autocast-on-CUDA path exactly as they are.
